p: Bristol has a knack for big, brilliant days out, and adventure golf slots in neatly alongside them. Aviation fans can head north to Aerospace Bristol in Filton, where the last Concorde to fly sits in its own hangar and you can actually walk through it. In August, the Bristol International Balloon Fiesta fills the skies above Ashton Court Estate, which is a cracking spot for a walk at any time of year.

Before you tee off, a few practical pointers. Allow roughly an hour for a round, plus time for a drink or a snack afterwards. If you've got a group of more than six, consider splitting into two teams so nobody is stood around waiting too long. And get the kids involved in choosing the order of play: it's amazing how much smoother things go when they feel in charge.

Bristol is also the home of Aardman Animations, the studio behind Wallace and Gromit, and you'll spot Gromit sculptures and nods to the famous duo around the city from time to time. For a bite to eat, St Nicholas Market in the old city is a great place to graze, with plenty of street food stalls and independent traders under one roof.

Fancy a view? Cabot Tower on Brandon Hill gives you a cracking panorama over the harbour and rooftops, and it's a short walk from Park Street. Put it all together and you've got a day out that really shows off the city.
